cohort: 83 pregnant women diagnosed with cancer during pregnancy, compared with matched controls without cancer diagnoses, out of a screened population of 80,524 pregnant women
finding: While chemotherapy during pregnancy was associated with reduced maternal mortality, no significant differences were found in children's mortality or developmental outcomes (ASQ) between women with cancer during pregnancy and those without.
mod_finding: Pregnant women with cancer had a higher cesarean rate (84.7% vs 52.5%, P=0.001) compared to matched controls.
